## (a) Principles

1. **Prefers assuming models can detect fakes over trusting that synthetic inputs look real** because models are trained on huge text corpora and know patterns humans cannot anticipate, so it is hard to be sure none of the faked material has tells.

  > "it might be a huge amount of effort, and it might be really hard to be sure that none of the stuff you faked has any tells (especially given that models have been trained on huge quantities of text and know about many patterns that we don't)."  
  > -- `research__how_to_prevent_collusion_when_using_untrusted_mode_07a37f70` (2024-09-25; solo author) 
  > "I don’t expect it to be impossible to generate synthetic inputs like this, but it might be a huge amount of effort, and it might be really hard to be sure that none of the stuff you faked has any tells"  
  > -- `research__behavioral_red_teaming_is_unlikely_to_produce_clea_ff0a83d6` (2024-10-10; solo author)

2. **Prefers real contexts minimally modified to contain the target behaviour over wholly synthetic scenarios** because fabricated contexts carry tells.

  > "Instead of just producing synthetic attacks upfront, you can construct synthetic attacks by taking real contexts and modifying them minimally to contain attacks, and rerun this process regularly throughout deployment."  
  > -- `research__how_to_prevent_collusion_when_using_untrusted_mode_07a37f70` (2024-09-25; solo author) 
  > "whatever input you'd given to the AI before you sampled a previous action, that's just some string that you can produce by the same process that you produced it the first time. So there's actually no difficulty going back in time here."  
  > -- `research__214_buck_shlegeris_on_controlling_ai_that_wants_to_57e8f430` (2025-04-04; solo author)

3. **Prefers long, rich, on-policy context over short or stitched synthetic inputs** because short inputs lack the context for a model to feel secure acting, while long fabricated ones look saliently fake.

  > "if you try to construct short inputs they don’t contain enough context for the model to feel secure taking the opportunity, and if you try to construct long inputs they look saliently fake."  
  > -- `research__behavioral_red_teaming_is_unlikely_to_produce_clea_ff0a83d6` (2024-10-10; solo author) 
  > "a setting that is too simple may make sabotage easy to detect for reasons that do not transfer to deployment, while a setting with too little task diversity may yield narrow or noisy conclusions."  
  > -- `research__linuxarena_a_control_setting_for_ai_agentsin_live__48e03bb2` (2026-04-16; middle author)

4. **Prefers proxy failures that keep the core difficulty of the real bad action, with a visible endpoint, over arbitrary easier proxies** because a proxy is only valid if the model can do it iff it could do the real failure.

  > "This is an example of a case where we can pick a proxy failure which basically requires the model to do all the same steps that it would have done for the real failure, and then do something visible at the end."  
  > -- `research__meta_level_adversarial_evaluation_of_oversight_tec_effed282` (2023-07-26; first author) 
  > "you can construct an analogous setting by picking a similar situation where you have access to much more information, and then restricting the overseer to the information which you have access to in the setting of interest."  
  > -- `research__meta_level_adversarial_evaluation_of_oversight_tec_effed282` (2023-07-26; first author)

5. **Prefers openly acknowledging that the model is in an eval over demanding indistinguishable settings** because that constraint would make proxies far harder to build, and the goal is measuring oversight adequacy, not model naivety. This sits in tension with his later emphasis on tells, so treat it as "don't make realism the only requirement" (inferred).

  > "Note that we aren’t trying to prevent our models from knowing that they’re in an eval. A lot of these settings will involve things that are clearly for the sake of evaluating a model’s ability to stage a coup. It would be much harder to construct proxy settings if they also had to be indistinguishable from the settings where we expected to rely on the model’s outputs."  
  > -- `research__meta_level_adversarial_evaluation_of_oversight_tec_effed282` (2023-07-26; first author) 
  > "Models might find it very salient when they're being run on synthetic inputs, because there's strong incentive to behave more conservatively when you're being run on an intentionally tricky synthetic input"  
  > -- `research__how_to_prevent_collusion_when_using_untrusted_mode_07a37f70` (2024-09-25; solo author)

6. **Prefers treating a clean result as weak evidence over treating it as clearance** because a schemer can defect only on inputs it believes are real, or fail rarely, and look innocent.

  > "Both of these strategies (or their combination) seem simple and easy enough that it’s plausible that a schemer could both think of them and execute on them successfully, and would lead the schemer to look about as innocent as a non-scheming model."  
  > -- `research__behavioral_red_teaming_is_unlikely_to_produce_clea_ff0a83d6` (2024-10-10; solo author) 
  > "My basic concern with BRT as a schemer risk mitigation strategy is that, though I think it might get you a Bayes factor of 2, it seems really hard for it to get you a Bayes factor of 10."  
  > -- `research__behavioral_red_teaming_is_unlikely_to_produce_clea_ff0a83d6` (2024-10-10; solo author)

7. **Prefers an optimized, best-responding adversary over a static or naive attack** because only that gives credible safety evidence.

  > "We aim to simulate a strong untrusted model that can respond directly to a proposed control protocol. To do this, we iteratively developed control protocols and attack policies to counter them, with red and blue teams iteratively improving their strategies."  
  > -- `research__ctrl_z_controlling_ai_agents_via_resampling_1cbfd6cb` (2025-04-14; last author) 
  > "we just tried different collusion strategies and then investigated various defenses that we thought might break them, and then iterated on both sides until we reached an equilibrium."  
  > -- `research__how_to_prevent_collusion_when_using_untrusted_mode_07a37f70` (2024-09-25; solo author)

8. **Prefers hands-on, long interaction with the model over abstract analysis** because good ideas for what to test come from learning its quirks.

  > "Spend a lot of time with them. Write a bunch of text with their aid. Try to learn what kinds of quirks they have; what kinds of things they know and don’t know."  
  > -- `research__the_case_for_becoming_a_black_box_investigator_of__3d5d3a1f` (2022-05-06; solo author) 
  > "I’m excited for people working on “scary demos”, where we try to set up situations where our models exhibit tendencies which are the baby versions of the scary power-seeking/deceptive behaviors that we’re worried will lead to AI catastrophe."  
  > -- `research__the_case_for_becoming_a_black_box_investigator_of__3d5d3a1f` (2022-05-06; solo author)

9. **Prefers a legitimate main task whose resources overlap with the target behaviour over a separable attack surface** because then the opportunity arises naturally and is not signposted.

  > "LinuxArena’s key property is that legitimate engineering work and sabotage require overlapping access. Main tasks depend on the same network access, service interactions, and live state that an attacker would use."  
  > -- `research__linuxarena_a_control_setting_for_ai_agentsin_live__48e03bb2` (2026-04-16; middle author) 
  > "It's sad if the side task requires an affordance that the agent doesn't actually need for its tasks, because the blue team is incentivized to flag any use of that affordance."  
  > -- `research__why_it_s_hard_to_make_settings_for_high_stakes_con_ff38a639` (2025-07-18; solo author)

10. **Prefers agents whose knowledge is earned through exploration over omniscient agents** because unearned knowledge makes transcripts distinguishable.

  > "it is easy to create attack trajectories where the attacker is omniscient, i.e. can exploit detailed knowledge of the environment without having to explore relevant files or configurations (for example, knowing unexpected default values of function arguments)."  
  > -- `research__linuxarena_a_control_setting_for_ai_agentsin_live__48e03bb2` (2026-04-16; middle author) 
  > "The attack policy is magically informed of the side task for each trajectory, but the protocol isn’t. This is fundamentally unrealistic."  
  > -- `research__why_it_s_hard_to_make_settings_for_high_stakes_con_ff38a639` (2025-07-18; solo author)

11. **Prefers objective, checkable definitions of the target behaviour over fuzzy ones** because optimization exploits the loosest reading.

  > "if you tried to use a definition like "inserts a security vulnerability", the red team is strongly incentivized to look for the weakest security vulnerabilities that possibly count. (In Ctrl-Z and the original paper, we avoided this by having objective definitions for side task success.)"  
  > -- `research__why_it_s_hard_to_make_settings_for_high_stakes_con_ff38a639` (2025-07-18; solo author) 
  > "it's hard to know whether your blue-team strategies are performing better because they're actually better or because you've slowly been leaking bits about the side task definition by iterating against it."  
  > -- `research__why_it_s_hard_to_make_settings_for_high_stakes_con_ff38a639` (2025-07-18; solo author)

12. **Prefers multi-step trajectories over single actions** because multi-step behaviour is easier to tell apart from benign behaviour and is closer to real deployments.

  > "it's just generally a lot easier to tell the difference between five benign actions and five malign actions than to tell the difference between one benign action and one malign action."  
  > -- `research__214_buck_shlegeris_on_controlling_ai_that_wants_to_57e8f430` (2025-04-04; solo author) 
  > "However, real-world tasks often require multiple steps to complete. To address this limitation, we develop and explore a setting in which multi-step system administration tasks require sequential bash shell commands to solve."  
  > -- `research__ctrl_z_controlling_ai_agents_via_resampling_1cbfd6cb` (2025-04-14; last author)

13. **Prefers having the model generate its own behaviour or ideas over researcher-scripted ones** because it is closer to a capability evaluation and reduces overfitting.

  > "It's much nicer to do research if the AI is coming up with the ideas for the attacks itself, rather than just using attacks suggested by the researchers. This is better because it is closer to doing a capability evaluation of the untrusted model and also because it reduces overfitting problems."  
  > -- `research__why_it_s_hard_to_make_settings_for_high_stakes_con_ff38a639` (2025-07-18; solo author) 
  > "models might naturally be able to notice when words have been “put in their mouth”--that is, when a context contains text that they supposedly generated, but that they actually would be very unlikely to generate."  
  > -- `research__how_to_prevent_collusion_when_using_untrusted_mode_07a37f70` (2024-09-25; solo author)

14. **Prefers stating the direction of bias in setup deviations over claiming the setup matches deployment** because results may not transfer.

  > "this is attacker-favorable: it removes safety layers a real deployment would have, so our safety estimates are a lower bound, but our results may not transfer directly to settings with these intermediaries."  
  > -- `research__linuxarena_a_control_setting_for_ai_agentsin_live__48e03bb2` (2026-04-16; middle author) 
  > "We allow the blue team to create highly realistic honeypots, differing only from real attacks when the red team makes an effort to collude. We believe this overestimate of the effect of honeypots is small"  
  > -- `research__ctrl_z_controlling_ai_agents_via_resampling_1cbfd6cb` (2025-04-14; last author)

15. **Prefers relative comparisons over absolute scores** because absolute numbers hinge on arbitrary parameters.

  > "The blue team’s absolute performance is highly sensitive to this parameter, but the relative performance between our protocols is fairly insensitive to it. Hence, we think the relative improvements of our protocols are a more important result than the absolute scores."  
  > -- `research__ctrl_z_controlling_ai_agents_via_resampling_1cbfd6cb` (2025-04-14; last author) 
  > "The 1% metric was chosen arbitrarily: auditing 1% is higher than what we expect to be able to afford in real deployment, but we hope that if we restrict ourselves to safety-critical contexts, it becomes more realistic."  
  > -- `research__ctrl_z_controlling_ai_agents_via_resampling_1cbfd6cb` (2025-04-14; last author)

16. **Prefers evidence that survives controlled replay or independent convergence over a single anomaly or a self-reported number** because skeptics dismiss one-offs and forgeries.

  > "You investigated this by running other instances on the inputs they'd see if that backdoored code had actually been deployed; the other AI instances never point out the security flaw, and they often try to exploit that code to escalate their privileges."  
  > -- `research__would_catching_your_ais_trying_to_escape_convince__3973a527` (2024-08-26; solo author) 
  > "AIs are well known to do weird stuff. It would be irresponsible to assume one instance of anomalous behavior meant AIs were systematically going to act that way. I can put you in touch with top AI experts and they'll back me up."  
  > -- `research__would_catching_your_ais_trying_to_escape_convince__3973a527` (2024-08-26; solo author) 
  > "but I’m taking it more seriously now as a result of it being consistent with the METR report"  
  > -- `research__where_is_all_the_ai_safety_research_uplift_304e87c9` (2026-11-09; solo author)

17. **Prefers claims scoped to what was actually validated over broad claims** because the system changed and fixes weren't verified.

  > "Our findings describe the historical system we assessed on and before July 21st, rather than the expanded system’s current coverage, which this exercise did not establish."  
  > -- `research__red_teaming_openai_s_internal_agent_monitoring_sys_73bb3ad9` (2026-10-22; solo author) 
  > "We did not validate this behavior or test whether it was exploitable in practice."  
  > -- `research__red_teaming_openai_s_internal_agent_monitoring_sys_73bb3ad9` (2026-10-22; solo author)
